Extensive DebitBit Overanalysis

Filed under: #translation

Introduction

On October 14th, 2026, I published a post analyzing DebitBit to Tumblr and I decided I would also post it on my website. This is a "sequel" to my post about Ongentoro. Currently the formatting is kind of bad because I just copied and pasted it directly from Tumblr but I will format it better soon OK thanks

Title

The first thing I thought when I saw the title "DebitBit" was, what the fuck is a debit bit?

And… this is a little play on words using "debit" and "bit" (=small amount of something). I also think "debit" can be interpreted as "de-bit," even though it would not be pronounced like that (you'd write de-bit as ディビット in Japanese). 

Officially, the English title is DebitBit, so that's how it's written here.

The title will make more sense to you once you finish this post (hopefully).

Song and MV: in general

I love it. It reminds me of Loveit? by biz and ZERA featuring LOLUET.

The composition is strange and exactly the kind of music that I love to listen to, so when I heard it for the first time I was absolutely enamored with it. The MV is perfectly complementary in weirdness.

There's a lack of color, like in Ongentoro, with black, white (more of an off-white blue-greenish color), and red being the only colors used. It fits the song. After all, red is the color of blood!

One word that I'd use to describe both the song and music video is grotesque. On VocaDB, one of the tags for DebitBit is "eroguro." I get this tag. It is a little erotic.

And that's the reason why everyone has been freaking out about Calogado (Yamai) online. They're super sexy and dosukebe*. A dosukebe nurse, if you will.

See, I've been saying Yamai was my favorite Calogado design for a while, but it took everyone else a couple months to catch up to me. That's no problem for me — I'm an early innovator.

One of my favorite parts of the MV isn't a part of the MV at all: it's how avogado6 released pretty much every single asset for DebitBit for free on their website! You can experiment with the music, illustration, and even the DaVinci Resolve project!

*do is an intensifier. So dosukebe might be "super pervert(ed)."

Lyrics & Romanization & Translation & Analysis

Lyrics/romanization/translation in green; notes are in whatever color your text normally is. Reminder: I am not fluent in Japanese, I'm a hobbyist trying their best. Please feel free to correct me if you see any issues.

Please also note that everything is my interpretation. I am not being 100% definitive, I just don't want to keep using "I think" or "probably" etc.

Firstly, the song starts us out with some samples from Calogado (Yamai)'s EX folder. These are the sneezing sounds at the beginning, if you didn't know. Well... you know now!

はーい口開けてー
汚い言葉の歯石が取れないね～

haai kuchi aketee
kitanai kotoba no shiseki ga torenai nee

Okay, keep your mouth agape.
I can't scrape tartar off dirty words you say, eh?

I wanted to see if l I could keep the flow and meaning intact, so I've tried my best to make it work as well in English as it does in Japanese.

For example, to preserve flow, I've made Calogado Canadian. Us Americans can't always be the center (or should I say centre?) of attention.

The font in DebitBit is kind of strange, and it makes 歯 look like the archaic kanji (kyuujitai form) 齒.

Both are pronounced the same and mean the same thing (tooth). 齒 is still used in Chinese (both traditional and simplified; simplification is different in Japan and China).

This song is about bad habits/addictions. More specifically, it's about how they break down your body and mental state to the point of no return. Calogado's simultaneously your nurse and a representation of your addictions/bad habits taking control of your life.

While some things listed in this song aren't addictive, just bad for you, I'll use "addiction" as a shorthand.

The reason you (I'm going to say "you" are the guy shackled to the bed in the MV) are in the hospital is because you are recovering from addiction. You're shackled to the bed, like how people are "shackled" to their addictions.

Money is used as a metaphor for your health. So a "debit," here, is something that costs you your health.

While the song has a sickness/illness theme, you aren't actually (that) sick. As one commenter says:

ずっと病院のベッドにいる主人公に咳以外の病気要素？が見つからないのが、「些細なことで休む権利がほしい(または些細なことをおおごとにする)」みたいな感じがあって、個人的にはとても面白いなと感じた。

The bed-bound protagonist doesn't seem to have any other illness besides a cough, so the "I want the right to rest for trivial things (or to make a huge deal out of trivialities)" sort of feeling, personally I found it very interesting.

I can't scrape tartar off dirty words you say, eh? is Calogado saying "your words can never be taken back once you say them." (Tartar can easily be removed by a dentist, but memories? not so easily!) If you've ever been alive, you'll know addicts tend to lie and say hurtful things.

はーい遠く見てー
悲しい現実直視できてないね～

haai tooku mite
kanashii genjitsu choukushi dekitenai nee

Okay, look far away.
You can't gaze at your pitiful reality, eh?

The font makes 視 look like 視. This is another older variant of the same kanji.

If you can't make out the text on the eye test, it's 現実 (genjitsu, reality).

Dissociation from reality is another theme of this song that's shown through its lyrics, composition, and music video. Even the font is weird!

はーい手開いてー
スマホと孤独を握って離さないね～

haai te hiraitee
sumaho to kodaku o nigitte hanasenai nee

Okay, open your hands.
Your phone and loneliness are held and won't separate, eh?

Phones make you lonely despite being made to connect people. Many people also have a phone addiction, so they can't separate themselves from their phones. I'm addicted to my laptop, which is different.

はーい顔出してー
良いね！実家に顔出さないのにね～

haai kaodashitee
iine! jikka ni kaodasenai noni nee

Okay, show me your face.
Yay! But you haven't shown it to your family in ages, eh?

Addicts tend to withdraw from society. Their family members may also choose to go no contact with them.

口内炎の数を数えて

kounaien no kazu o kazoete

I'll count the amount of mouth ulcers you have.

Count and amount both end in -ount, like how kazu and kazoete sound similar and use the same kanji.

カロリー　カフェイン　脂質　糖質
好きでしょう？ねえ好きでしょう？

karorii kafein shishitsu doushitsu
suki deshou? nee suki deshou?

Calories, caffeine, lipids, carbs;
you like those, right? Hey. You like those, right?

I'm not sure if it's accidentally or on purpose, but the suki deshou? nee suki deshou? is similar to the ii desho? nee ii desho? in Ongentoro. I've decided to translate them similarly, too. Not like there's many other directions you can go, though.

ポテチ　エナドリ　ラーメン　お酒
好きでしょう？ねえ好きでしょう？

potechi enadori raamen osake
suki deshou? nee suki deshou?

Potato chips, energy drinks, ramen, alcohol;
you like those, right? Hey. You like those, right?

ゲーム　タバコ　SNS　夜更かし
好きでしょう？ねえ好きでしょう？

geemu tabako netto yafukashi
suki deshou? nee suki deshou?

Video games, cigarettes, the internet, staying up late;
you like those, right? Hey. You like those, right?

Read as "SNS" (social networking service: social media) but pronounced as "internet" (netto). This change is kind of interesting to me since ネット could fit where "SNS" is on Calogado's torso.

To be fair, one of the first things you think when you think "internet" isn't Wikipedia, or online dictionaries, or Steam. Social media is basically what the internet is at this point...

自堕落　寝不足　サボり　横着
好きでしょう？デビットビット

jidaraku nebusoku sabori ouchaku
suki deshou? debitto bitto

Decadence, sleep deprivation, procrastination, laziness;
you like those, right? Debit bit

自堕落 means self-indulgence, and "decadence" also means self-indulgence… when used positively. When used negatively, however, it describes decay or deterioration (due to self-indulgence).

I thought this was interesting, and fit the song well, so I used a bit of a non-standard translation.

サボる (saboru) also can mean to skip work/school entirely.

はーい声出してー
聞き返されないよう腹から出して～

haai koe dashitee
kikikaesarenai you hara kara dashitee

Okay, open up and say
Say your true feelings so you won't repeat yourself again

はーい上向いてー
太陽の下で歩く練習して～

haai uwa muitee
taiyou no shita de aruku renshuu shitee

Okay, look up at space
and learn how to walk beneath the sun's rays

It's really just "okay, look up" but I've tried to rhyme it

You're a NEET and don't spend a lot of time outside. (NEET is also one of the tags on VocaDB for this song.)

はーいよく聞いてー
都合の悪い報告もよく聞いて～

haai yoku kiitee
tsugo no warui houkoku mo yoku kiitee

Okay, listen closely.
Listen closely to my inconvenient reports, too.

The first line, はーいよく聞いてー, is Calogado (Kasuka)'s only line in the song, and it's a good one!

はーい考えてー
前借健康返却考えて～

haai kangaetee
maegari kenkou henkyaku kangaetee

Okay, go and contemplate
Contemplate getting an advance on your health

The dictionary will tell you 前借 is zenshaku, and normally that's true, but it's pronounced like maegari here. In other words, it's pronounced as if it was written 前借り.

Obviously, you can't get an advance on your health. Calogado's teasing you for not taking good care of your body.

Here's an interesting comment that I saw:

デビットは銀行口座などの「引き落とし」、ビットは「最小単位」を意味してて 「健康を前借して生きている状態がいずれ口座から引き落とされる」って感じで1:05の歌詞にあってて好き

A "debit" is a withdrawal from a bank account, and "bit" is "the smallest amount," so I like the lyrics' feeling at 1:05 of "living by borrowing health will eventually put your account into debt."

Health is money, your account is your life...and "debt" is death. You'll die if you keep indulging yourself. Even small amounts add up. Something like that.

(This is 1:05, by the way.)

他人の引き出物
君の吹き出物

hito no hikidemono
kimi no fukidemono

People's wedding favors
are your rash.

他人 is spelled as tanin (other people), but pronounced as hito (people).

During this part in the MV, Calogado goes ahead and circles ご欠席 (gokesseki, not attending)* for you.

I touched on it previously, but this is another social isolation thing. You can't attend weddings, nor can you be happy for others.

*ご (go) or お (o) before a word (御 in kanji for both) just makes the word more formal. 

野菜　お魚　ぬるま湯　薬
嫌いでしょう？ねえ嫌いでしょう？

yasai osakana nurumayu kusuri
kirai deshou? nee kirai deshou?

Vegetables, fish, a boring life, medicine;
you hate those, right? Hey. You hate those, right?

ぬるま湯 is literally "lukewarm water," but used figuratively to mean a boring/dull life. "Lukewarm" in English is also used similarly.

ビタミン　ミネラル　酵素　鉄分
嫌いでしょう？ねえ嫌いでしょう？

bitamin mineraru kouso tetsubun
kirai deshou? nee kirai deshou?

Vitamins, minerals, enzymes, irons;
you hate those, right? Hey. You hate those, right?

早寝　早起き　勉強　運動
嫌いでしょう？ねえ嫌いでしょう？

hayane hayaoki benkyou undou
kirai deshou? nee kirai deshou?

Early to bed, early to rise, studying, exercise;
you hate those, right? Hey. You hate those, right?

掃除　洗濯　社交　身支度
嫌いでしょう？ねえ嫌いでしょう？

souji sentaku shakou mijitaku
kirai deshou? nee kirai deshou?

Cleaning, laundry, social interaction, dressing yourself;
you hate those, right? Hey. You hate those, right?

『微細な負債　このくらいいいかって　見送りを　見送り続けて』
「バター　砂糖　醤油　マヨネーズ　塩 生クリーム　ニンニク　マーガリン」
(お好きでしょう？ねえ好きでしょう？)

『sasai na fusai kono kurai iika tte mioku o mioku tsuzukete』
「bataa satou shouyu mayoneezu shio namakuriimu nikuniku maagarin」(osuki deshou? nee suki deshou?)

『an insignificant debt, "this much is okay" you say, letting go and moving on』
「butter, sugar, soy sauce, salt, fresh cream, garlic, margarine」
(You love those, right? Hey. You like those, right?)

The lyrics here are choppy and strange on purpose, to represent your mind and body breaking down. So if the translation makes little sense, that's not me. Mostly.

微細 is written as bisai but pronounced as 些細 (sasai). bisai means "very small," while sasai is more like "so small that it's unimportant or trivial." It's a more negative word.

I will insist on the interpretation that "debt" is not monetary debt. Addictions can start like, "well, if I do it just one time..." ("this much is okay" you say, letting go and moving on)

『積み重なって　膨れ上がって　返せなくって　逃げるしかなくて』
「ケーキ　ピザ　コーラ　アイスクリーム　油そば　揚げ物 チーズ　焼肉」
(お好きでしょう？ねえ好きでしょう？)

『tsumi kasanatte fukure agatte kaesenakutte nigeru shikanakute』
「keeki piza koora aisukuriimu aburasoba agemono chiizu yakiniku」
(osuki deshou? nee suki deshou?)

『it piles up, swells up, can't pay it back, can only run away』
「cake, pizza, soda, ice cream, aburasoba, deep-frying, cheese, yakiniku」
(You love those, right? Hey. You like those, right?)

The addiction quickly becomes too much to control, and you're too deep into it (it piles up, swells up, can't pay it back). You try to quit your addiction (run away).

『養生今更　手続きどれだ　重い体じゃ　追手巻けぬまま』
「散財　ギャンブル　効率　ハイエナ　強者　名誉　正義　破滅」
(お好きでしょう？ねえ好きでしょう？)

『yousei imasara tetsuzuki doreda omoi karada ja oite makenumama』
「sanzai gyanburu kouritsu haiena kyousha meiyo seigi hametsu」
(osuki deshou? nee suki deshou?)

『a positive result too late, which procedures should you take, your heavy body, it shan't outmaneuver your pursuers still』
「splurging, gambling, efficiency, vultures, strong people, honor, justice, destruction」
(You love those, right? Hey. You like those, right?)

養生 (youjyou, taking care of one's health) is pronounced here as ようせい (yousei) which has multiple different definitions, but I'd say "positive" is the most likely one (as in "positive result").

ぬ is an archaic way of negating, so I used "shan't" here.

In Japanese, the word hyena can be used to mean "a person who swarms around defenseless people or organizations to use them for profit." Vulture is a similar word (they're both animals!) that conveys a similar meaning in English.

Even though you quit, it's too late (a positive result too late). You've already dug your own grave: your mental state is exhausted, and you can't continue further.

『内臓とられ　おけらになって　ご臨終さま』
「治療　治療　治療　治療　治療　治療」

『naizou torare okera ni natte gorinjuusama』
「chiryou chiryou chiryou chiryou chiryou chiryou」

『entrails coming out, becoming broke, on your deathbed』
「treatment treatment treatment treatment treatment treatment」

I wanted to use the grossest word for 内蔵, so I asked my Twitter followers "is viscera or entrails grosser?" and they said "entrails." It was an overwhelming "entrails" victory.

a lot　デビットビット

a lot debitto bitto

a lot debit bit

After this, you wake up! (Calogado was nice enough to give you an injection.) Was it… all a dream!? If you watch the video on Niconico Douga, many comments that ask "夢オチ？！" (yumeochi) will start to appear. As the Wiktionary article says, this is the term for a "was it all a dream?" ending.

But then! Calogado appears right above you. It's an open-ended ending!

Like, for example, how someone believes they have recovered from their addiction but then are dragged right back into it. Perhaps? Perchance? Or am I overthinking this one?

Final Thoughts

I wish Calogado was MY NURSE!!! Gah! Calogado, wait for me, the hospital is not too far! If you see me in a hospital room locked up with Calogado, don't help me, I'm exactly where I want to be!!!

We all can't get what we want in this life, though, and I'm unfortunately in the universe where Calogado is not real. Maybe next time.

An aside: why's DebitBit so popular!?

Okay. I want to talk about this. I need to talk about it so bad. 

Something that surprised me about DebitBit was its immediate popularity. The first preview has 76k likes on Twitter. The second has 46k; the third 40k; the fourth 24k; and the "DebitBit WIP 1" 40 second audio has 72k. It's mental.

Even avogado6 is surprised at its popularity, particularly on TikTok, a platform they had to make an account on recently to prevent DebitBit reuploads.

It's topped the Niconico Vocaloid Songs top 20 chart for three weeks in a row.

So, I've been wondering. Why did it blow up!? 

I've thought about it for a while and came up with a couple of reasons.

  1. Calogado (Yamai)

Despite no one knowing who Calogado is, their sexiness and dosukebe-ness have propelled DebitBit to immense popularity. (As I've already mentioned.) The, um, most attractive character in fiction, if you will.

I see them often referred to as "the nurse," which is not their name — their name's Calogado. But Calogado's been getting a lot more popular because of DebitBit!

There's even a small anglophone fandom for them on Twitter. Before, I could count the number of English-speaking Calogado fans on my hands, but now I'd need a few extra hands.

2. Song's good

It really fucking is.

2a. It's exactly the kind of song TikTokers like

Let me draw your attention to a YouTube comment I saw. (can't find the link RIP but it existed at some point please believe me)

全体的に音がずっと絶えなくて画面も情報量が多いドパガキ向けの動画だから「この曲好きでしょう？」って言われてる気がして良き

Generally, this is a bunch of constant noise and overstimulating images, it's a video that's geared towards dopagaki so "you like this song, right?" is basically what it's saying and it's so good

And this is exactly what I feel, too. The reason why it's popular on TikTok is because it's dopagaki-core. I don't mean this as a bad thing. As I said, DebitBit is insanely good; loud and in-your-face stuff is my favorite thing ever.

And stuff that's popular on TikTok is also popular everywhere else since TikTok is used by basically everyone. …Except me, I don't use it. Hasn't Used TikTok Since The Furry Wars of 2019 Award.

3. It's memetic

I mentioned before that avogado6 released pretty much every single DebitBit asset to the public. It's so easy to make covers with it, so you see it everywhere.

4. avogado6

is an extremely popular illustrator, so anything they make is going to have at least a little motion to begin with. 

I thought Ongentoro was going to be Calogado's most popular song until DebitBit released.

5. Luck

Everything that blows up online needs a little RNG.
